newsitem.title: USA: Dairy Mart to assess value of assets.
newsitem.headline: Dairy Mart to assess value of assets.

text.p: Dairy Mart Convenience Stores Inc said it hired Oppenheimer & Co to assess the value of its assets in the northeastern United States to aid the company in determining their fair value.
"We have not made a formal decision to sell our assets in the Northeast, nor has any offer been made for them," Robert Stein Jr, chairman, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Dairy Mart, which has a total of 870 outlets, said the assessment is for its 170 locations in Connecticut, Massachusetts, Rhode Island and New York. Of the 170, 55 of the convenience stores sell gasoline.
The company's strongest concentration of stores is in the Midwest with 700 stores, Dairy Mart said. The company intends to move its headquarters to Ohio in 1997, it said.

Asessing the value of its assets in the Northeast will enable the company to plan corporate strategies more effectively and give the company a better idea whether any offer to buy its stores would be worth exploring, Dairy Mart said.
Dairy Mart had previously announced a five-year, $100 million store-improvement program funded from cash flow.
